CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Judy Gomez is a 64-year-old female with psoriatic arthritis presenting for ongoing management. She has been tapered down on prednisone and is currently taking 1 mg daily, which she reports is adequate. She occasionally takes an extra dose approximately once weekly when experiencing increased pain in her feet, particularly on days when she is more active. She has a desk job. She reports that methotrexate has been helpful for her joint pain. She did not take methotrexate during the week of her first COVID vaccine dose due to concerns about vaccine efficacy interference. She reported feeling significantly worse that week and resumed the medication. She continued methotrexate for her second COVID vaccine dose per hotline recommendation. She reports the recent increase in methotrexate has improved her knee pain. She is concerned about bruising that appears after minor trauma without pain sensation preceding the bruising.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Joint pain in hands and feet. Bruising with minor trauma. Nail ridges noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily.
Methotrexate.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a desk job. More pain with increased physical activity on days off.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Shoes and socks removed. Small joint pain in hands. Joint pain in feet. Knee flexion with good range of motion, improved from prior. Good toe flexion with full range of motion. Nail ridges present consistent with psoriasis.

RESULTS
Blood work to be scheduled for monitoring given methotrexate use.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis, improving on current regimen. Discontinue prednisone. Continue methotrexate. Schedule blood work at front desk. Bruising expected to improve with discontinuation of prednisone. Follow-up in 3 months.
